source.title: Problems and Conjectures Presented at the Third International Conference on Permutation Patterns (University of Florida, March 7-11, 2005)

accepted.question_text: Let B be a finite set of permutation patterns, let Av(B) be the class of permutations that avoid every pattern in B, and let s_n(B) be the number of permutations of length n in Av(B). A sequence is called P-recursive if it satisfies a linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients. Is the Noonan-Zeilberger conjecture false, and in particular is the sequence s_n(1324) not P-recursive?

evidence.quote: For a set of permutations B define Av(B) to be the set of permutations that avoid all of the permutations in B and let sn(B) denote the number of permutations of length n in Av(B).
A sequence sn is said to be P-recursive (which is short for polynomially recursive) if there are polynomials p0, p1, . . . pk so that pk(n)sn+k + pk−1(n)sn+k−1 + . . . + p0(n)sn = 0.
Conjecture (Doron Zeilberger): The Noonan-Zeilberger Conjecture is false, and, in particular, the sequence sn(1324) is not P-recursive.

accepted.question_text: Let C be a permutation class. What necessary and sufficient conditions characterize exactly which classes C have generating functions that are rational, algebraic, D-finite, or belong to other comparable regularity classes?
accepted.context_brief: Classifying permutation classes by generating-function type

evidence.quote: Problem (Doron Zeilberger): Find necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing the classes whose generating functions are: • rational, • algebraic, • D-finite, • . . .

accepted.question_text: A composition of n is a sequence a = (a1, a2, ..., ak) of positive integers with a1 + a2 + ... + ak = n, where order matters and the parts need not be distinct. Such a composition contains a permutation beta if it has a subsequence order-isomorphic to beta. Is the number of compositions of n into positive parts that avoid the pattern 123 a non-P-recursive sequence in n?

evidence.quote: We say that a contains the permutation β if it contains a subsequence that is order isomorphic to β.
$201 Conjecture (Herb Wilf): The number of 123-avoiding compositions of n into positive parts is not a P-recursive sequence.

accepted.question_text: For sets of permutation patterns B1 and B2, write B1 ∼ B2 when s_n(B1) = s_n(B2) for all natural numbers n, so that B1 and B2 are equally avoided. What necessary and sufficient conditions determine when two permutations are Wilf-equivalent?

evidence.quote: We say that the sets B1 and B2 are Wilf-equivalent, and write B1 ∼ B2, if sn(B1) = sn(B1) for all natural numbers n, that is, if B1 and B2 are equally avoided.
Problem: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for two permutations to be Wilf-equivalent.

accepted.question_text: Let pi be a permutation of length k, and let sigma_1, sigma_2, ..., sigma_k be permutations; write pi[sigma_1, sigma_2, ..., sigma_k] for the inflation obtained by replacing the i-th entry of pi by a block order-isomorphic to sigma_i so that the blocks themselves are order-isomorphic to pi. For arbitrary permutations sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3 and every natural number n, is it always true that s_n(132[sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3]) < s_n(123[sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3]), that s_n(312[sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3]) < s_n(123[sigma_1, sigma_2, sigma_3]), and, for every t at least 2, that s_n(123[sigma_1, 12...t, sigma_3]) < s_n(123[sigma_1, t...21, sigma_3])?

evidence.quote: We define the inflation of π by σ1, σ2, . . . , σk to be the permutation obtained by replacing the ith element of π by a block order isomorphic to σi so that the blocks themselves are order isomorphic to π. We write the resulting permutation as π[σ1, σ2, . . . , σk].

Conjecture (Alex Burstein): For any permutations σ1, σ2, σ3, and any natural number n, (1) sn(132[σ1, σ2, σ3]) < sn(123[σ1, σ2, σ3]), (2) sn(312[σ1, σ2, σ3]) < sn(123[σ1, σ2, σ3]), (3) sn(123[σ1, 12 . . . t, σ3]) < sn(123[σ1, t . . . 21, σ3]) for any t ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: A permutation is layered if it is the direct sum of finitely many decreasing permutations. Let pi be a nonlayered permutation in S_k, let sigma_1, sigma_2, ..., sigma_k be permutations, and let 12...k[sigma_1, sigma_2, ..., sigma_k] denote the inflation of the increasing permutation 12...k by those blocks. For every natural number n, is it always true that s_n(pi[sigma_1, sigma_2, ..., sigma_k]) < s_n(12...k[sigma_1, sigma_2, ..., sigma_k])?

evidence.quote: A permutation is said to be layered if it is the direct sum of some number of decreasing permutations.
Conjecture (Alex Burstein): For any nonlayered permutation π ∈ Sk, permutations σ1, σ2, . . . , σk, and natural numbers n, sn(π[σ1, σ2, . . . , σk]) < sn(12 . . . k[σ1, σ2, . . . , σk]).

accepted.question_text: For a permutation pi on [n], let P_pi be the poset on the values 1, ..., n ordered by i ≼ j when i ≤ j as integers and i occurs before j in pi; let conv(P) be the poset on the same elements in which i ≼_conv j exactly when the rank of i in P is at most the rank of j; and let conv(pi) be the unique layered permutation whose associated poset is isomorphic to conv(P_pi). Is it true that s_n(pi) ≤ s_n(conv(pi)) for every permutation pi and every natural number n?

evidence.quote: Given a poset P with rank function r, we let conv(P) denote the convex hull of P. The poset conv(P) is defined on the same set of elements as P, but in conv(P), i ≼conv j if and only if r(i) ≤ r(j) (in P).
For any permutation π there is a unique layered permutation, which we refer to as conv(π), such that Pπ ∼= Pconv(π).
Conjecture (Miklós Bóna): For any permutation π and natural number n, sn(π) ≤ sn(conv(π)).

accepted.question_text: For a set X of permutations of varying lengths, let gr(X) = lim sup_{n→∞} |X ∩ S_n|^{1/n}. Improve the current lower bound on gr(Av(1324)), the growth rate of the class of permutations avoiding 1324, using the Maple package WILFPLUS.
accepted.context_brief: Lower bounds for the growth rate of Av(1324)

evidence.quote: We define the upper growth rate of X to be gr(X) = lim sup n→∞ root_n |X ∩ Sn|.
$200 Problem (Doron Zeilberger): Improve on the AERWZ lower bound for gr(Av(1324)) using the Maple package WILFPLUS [25].

accepted.question_text: If B is a finite set of permutation patterns, does the limit gr(Av(B)) = lim_{n→∞} |Av(B) ∩ S_n|^{1/n} always exist?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of growth rates for finitely based classes

evidence.quote: It would be natural to define the growth rate of X as gr(X) = lim n→∞ root_n |X ∩ Sn|, but this limit is not known to exist in general.
Conjecture (Vince Vatter): For any finite set of patterns B, the growth rate of Av(B) exists.

accepted.question_text: An antichain of permutations is a set of permutations such that no permutation in the set contains another. How quickly can an antichain of permutations grow? More precisely, how large can gr(X) be when X is an antichain of permutations?
accepted.context_brief: Maximum possible growth of permutation antichains

evidence.quote: An antichain of permutations is a set of permutations such that no permutation contains another.
Problem (Michael Albert): How quickly can an antichain of permutations grow? More precisely, how large can gr(X) be for an antichain X?

accepted.question_text: For a permutation pi, let s(pi) be the output of the greedy stack-sorting algorithm, and call pi West t-stack sortable if s^t(pi) is the identity permutation. For which pairs (t, n) is the number of West t-stack sortable permutations of length n odd?
accepted.context_brief: Parity of West t-stack sortable permutations

evidence.quote: A permutation is West t-stack sortable if st(π) is the identity permutation.
Problem (Miklós Bóna): For which t, n is the number of West t-stack sortable permutations of length n an odd number?

accepted.question_text: Give a combinatorial proof that, for every integer k, the number of West 2-stack sortable permutations on 4k + 3 elements is even.

evidence.quote: Problem (Mikós Bóna): In particular, the number of West 2-stack sortable permutations on 4k + 3 elements is always even. Give a combinatorial proof.

accepted.question_text: Consider a general t-stack sorting machine, where one asks whether a given input permutation can be sorted using t stacks in series under some sequence of legal moves. Can this decision problem be solved in polynomial time, or is it NP-complete?

evidence.quote: By allowing any sorting algorithm we reach the definition of general t-stack sortability.
Problem (Mike Atkinson): Can one decide in polynomial time whether an input permutation is sortable by a general t-stack sorting machine, or is this problem NP-complete?

accepted.question_text: What is the shortest permutation that cannot be sorted by a general 3-stack sorting machine?
accepted.context_brief: Shortest unsortable permutation for three stacks

evidence.quote: Problem (Steve Waton): What is the shortest permutation that can not be sorted by a general 3-stack sorting machine?

trace.notes: Mapped an 8-page conference problem summary. Open-problem material is concentrated in Sections 2 through 5, on pages 2 through 7.
Section 2 yields three explicit open items about P-recursiveness and generating functions.
Section 3 yields one Wilf-equivalence problem and three comparison conjectures.
Section 4 yields three growth-rate problems and conjectures.
Section 5 yields four explicit stack-sorting problems.
Inlined the meanings of Av(B), s_n(B), and P-recursiveness so the Zeilberger conjecture is self-contained.
Rephrased the research program as a standalone classification question for permutation classes.
Expanded the composition-avoidance conjecture by inlining the definition of containment for compositions.
Made the Wilf-equivalence problem standalone by including the equality condition on avoidance counts.
Converted Burstein's three-part conjecture into a single self-contained question about inflated patterns.
Inlined the notion of layered permutations to state the nonlayered-versus-layered inflation conjecture without source references.
Expanded conv(pi) using the convex-hull poset construction described in the source.
Restated the AERWZ lower-bound problem using the source's growth-rate notation.
Rewrote the growth-rate existence conjecture as an explicit limit-existence question.
Inlined the definition of antichain to make the growth question self-contained.
Included the definition of West t-stack sortability in the parity question.
Preserved the specific parity claim for lengths 4k+3 and restated it as a standalone proof problem.
Expanded the algorithmic question to specify the decision problem for general t-stack machines.
Kept the shortest-unsortable-permutation problem as a direct standalone question.
